title: Elastic Beam Bending Simulator
prompt:
Create a 3D interactive cantilever beam bending simulator using Three.js. The entire application must be in a single HTML file.

## Three.js Import
Use this importmap in <head>:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
Then in <script type="module">:
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';

## Scene Setup
- Black background (0x111111).
- PerspectiveCamera at (15, 10, 15), looking at origin.
- OrbitControls for camera manipulation.
- Ambient light (0x404040) and directional light (0xffffff, intensity 1.0) at (10, 20, 10).
- A grid helper (size 30, divisions 30) at y=0.

## Beam Model
- A cantilever beam: fixed at the left end (x=0), free at the right end (x=10).
- Represent the beam as 20 connected box segments (each 0.5 wide, 0.3 tall, 1.0 deep).
- Undeformed beam lies along x-axis at y=2.
- The beam deforms according to Euler-Bernoulli theory: deflection y(x) = (F * x^2 * (3L - x)) / (6 * E * I), where L=10 (beam length), F=applied force, E=Young's modulus, I=moment of inertia (use I = 0.00225 for a 0.3x0.3 cross section).
- Color the beam segments by stress: low stress = blue (0x0066ff), high stress = red (0xff3300), interpolate by HSL.

## Controls
- A slider (id='slider-force', range 0 to 50, step 1, default 10) to set the applied point force F at the free end (in Newtons).
- A slider (id='slider-E', range 1000 to 100000, step 1000, default 20000) to set Young's modulus E.
- Press 'R' to reset both sliders to defaults.
- A label (id='label-force') showing current force value.
- A label (id='label-E') showing current E value.

## Visualization
- Show the applied force as a red arrow (ArrowHelper) at the beam tip pointing downward, scaled by force magnitude.
- Show a green sphere at the beam tip to mark the deflection point.
- Display a dashed reference line showing the undeformed beam position.

## HUD
- A semi-transparent panel (id='hud') in top-left showing:
  - Max deflection (id='hud-deflection'): tip deflection in units, 2 decimal places.
  - Force value (id='hud-force'): current F.
  - Young's modulus (id='hud-E'): current E.
  - Max stress (id='hud-stress'): approximate max bending stress = F*L / (E*I) * E, displayed to 1 decimal.
  - Segment count (id='hud-segments'): always 20.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame:
- `force`: number (current force F)
- `youngModulus`: number (current E)
- `tipDeflection`: number (deflection at x=L, rounded to 4 decimals)
- `maxStress`: number (max bending stress, rounded to 2 decimals)
- `segmentCount`: number (always 20)
- `tipPosition`: {x, y, z} (position of beam tip)
- `frameCount`: number (incremented each frame)
- `cameraDistance`: number (distance from camera to origin, rounded to 1 decimal)
- `isReset`: boolean (true if force=10 and E=20000)
- `barsValid`: boolean (true if no segment has NaN position)

Ensure the animation loop updates __3D_STATE__ every frame before rendering.
physics_constraints: Beam tip deflection must follow Euler-Bernoulli formula: y = FL^3/(3EI) at x=L within 5% tolerance. Deflection must increase monotonically with force. Deflection must decrease when E increases. No NaN in any segment position. Max stress must be positive when force > 0.
